{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-ex47","title":"DeadDrop OSCORE POST gate treats option presence as auth","description":"File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py
Perspective: security (also correctness)

Spec 18.9: writes MUST be OSCORE-protected; unprotected POST returns 4.01
{"error":"oscore_required"}. DeadDropResource.render_post uses
_request_context_id() as that gate.

_request_context_id() (lines 57-71) reads request.oscore_context,
request.oscore_context_id, and request.oscore_protected. The live CoAP
stack never sets those attributes (only tests set oscore_context_id).
It then treats request.opt.oscore is not None as authenticated and
returns context id "default".

Evidence: POST with valid SenML and request.opt.oscore=b"\x00" (no
OSCORE unprotect) returns 2.01 Created and stores the drop under
"default". An empty OSCORE option also passes.

Impact:
- Unprotected clients satisfy the MUST-protect rule by attaching an
  OSCORE option to plaintext.
- All such writes share context "default", so they share the 6/hour
  bucket and can GET private/group drops stored under "default".
- Per-context rate limits and private-drop ACL cannot work on the
  live stack because real OSCORE identities are never bound.

Contrast: HandoffResource documents that object_security is set only
after successful unprotect.

Acceptance: unprotected POST with a spoofed OSCORE option still
returns 4.01; only a request that actually unprotected under a
distinct OSCORE context is allowed, rate-limited, and used as the
private/group ACL key.

new_value: DeadDrop POST/GET OSCORE gate no longer treats opt.oscore or oscore_protected as auth. Only a non-empty identity bound after unprotect (request.oscore_context / oscore_context_id or the same on request.remote) is accepted as the rate-limit and private/group ACL key. Spoofed option (b'\x00' and empty), boolean flags, and empty ids return 4.01 oscore_required; tests in test_deaddrop_resource.py pass (42).
